Apis Partners Takes Majority Stake In Korridor To Expand Financial Services For African Freight Operators
By Amit Chowdhry
Today at 10:35 AM
Apis Partners Takes Majority Stake In Korridor To Expand Financial Services For African Freight Operators
Apis Partners has acquired a majority stake in Korridor, a Mauritius-based financial technology company that helps freight operators pay for cross-border journeys in Sub-Saharan Africa. Apis made the investment through Apis Growth Fund III, which held its final close at $1.23 billion in May 2026. The announcement did not disclose the purchase price.
Founded in 2007, Korridor operates across 13 countries with more than 360 network points. More than 2,200 customers and nearly 50,000 trucks use its network to handle costs that arise during freight journeys, including tolls, border fees, fuel, insurance and parking. Its platform also helps operators manage foreign exchange and track spending across their fleets.
Drivers have traditionally carried cash to cover expenses on multiday trips. Korridor gives fleet operators a way to make and track payments digitally in multiple currencies. It also offers tools for planning routes and gives participating suppliers access to customers traveling across borders.
Apis said it has followed Korridor since 2024 and will work with management to accelerate the company’s transition from a physical payments network to a digital platform. The investment will also support plans to expand credit and insurance services for fleet operators. Korridor’s existing role in managing routine freight payments gives it a way to offer those services to customers already using the platform.
KEY QUOTES
“Korridor already supports more than 2,200 customers and nearly 50,000 trucks across 13 countries, with a network of more than 360 network points built over nineteen years. What particularly attracted us was the opportunity to build on this established infrastructure and customer base by expanding the range of services available to fleet operators. By reducing reliance on cash, improving visibility and helping operators run their businesses more efficiently, Korridor is already delivering meaningful benefits to its customers today. For Apis, there is no trade-off between impact and financial returns, and we believe supporting businesses that solve real operational challenges creates the foundation for long-term growth.”
Udayan Goyal, Co-Founder And Managing Partner Of Apis Partners
“We’re delighted to partner with Korridor and build on the relationship we’ve developed with its management team over the past few years. The team has built a strong position in the market and driven the business’s digitalisation. Cross-border freight underpins trade across Africa, and Korridor has built a unique position within that ecosystem. This is exactly the kind of opportunity Apis looks for: a business delivering essential services today, with a clear opportunity to deepen its relationships with customers over time. We’ve successfully applied this playbook across multiple portfolio companies, helping businesses leverage trusted customer relationships and existing distribution networks to expand the services they provide. We look forward to supporting the team as they continue to grow the platform and broaden its impact across the region.”
Hossam Abou Moussa, Partner And Deputy CEO Of Apis Partners

The post Trump Accounts Draw More Than $1 Billion In Contributions From Friends And Family appeared first on Pulse 2.0 .
articles.text:
Trump Accounts Draw More Than $1 Billion In Contributions From Friends And Family
By Amit Chowdhry
Today at 9:57 AM
Trump Accounts Draw More Than $1 Billion In Contributions From Friends And Family
Trump Accounts has reported more than $1 billion in contributions from friends and family members to individual children’s accounts. More than 3 million people contributed. Total deposits exceeded $9 billion, including contributions from individual donors, major philanthropic gifts, and federal seed funding.
The $1 billion figure measures contributions made by friends and relatives to individual accounts. The broader deposit figure also includes philanthropic donations from organizations such as the Michael & Susan Dell Foundation and one-time contributions from the U.S. Department of the Treasury.
Trump Accounts are tax-advantaged investment accounts established for eligible children under 18 with a valid Social Security number. Children born from January 1, 2025, through December 31, 2028, are also eligible for a one-time $1,000 Treasury contribution.
A parent or guardian must claim a child’s account before managing it or enabling contributions from friends, relatives and employers. The program uses its official app to verify the adult’s identity and relationship to the child. The adult then reviews the child’s information and accepts the account terms. Once the account is claimed, friends and family members can use a QR code in the app to contribute directly.
The program’s announcement said friends and families can contribute up to $5,000 per year. Employers can contribute up to $2,500 per year within the overall $5,000 annual limit. Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent said President Donald Trump had also made personal donations to individual accounts during the week of the announcement.
KEY QUOTES
“Trump Accounts are a transformative government program for American children. It is the largest government start-up in American history. Adding to this effort is the extraordinary response from friends and family members of individual Trump Account holders, whose contributions have now surpassed $1 billion nationwide. Parents should download the Trump Accounts app today and claim their child’s account to watch their financial future grow.”
Frank J. Bisignano, Chief Executive Officer Of The Internal Revenue Service
“The American people are investing in Trump Accounts with a generosity that represents the finest instincts of our national character. President Trump wanted to make it especially easy to contribute to Trump Accounts, and friends and families across the country are seizing that opportunity to help the next generation build wealth from day one. This week, the President himself joined the millions of Americans who have made personal donations to individual Trump Accounts. With every contribution, we are bringing the promise of long-term financial security within reach of American children.”
Scott Bessent, U.S. Secretary Of The Treasury

articles.title: Lute’s CEO calls touch ‘the missing signal’ as it raises $20M
articles.snippet: Lute’s CEO calls touch ‘the missing signal’ as it raises $20M The Next Web
articles.text:
The Lute team with one of its robots.
Credit: Lute
Lute, a Warsaw physical AI startup founded in January, has raised $20M to build robot models trained on touch. The pre-seed and seed money was announced on Tuesday . OTB Ventures and FORWARD.one co-led the seed round, and Credo Ventures and Seedcamp led the pre-seed. Inovo VC, Borusan Ventures, ff Venture Capital and angel investor Naval Ravikant also took part.
Lute will spend the money on touch data, model training and new customers. It is hiring in Warsaw and San Mateo, California.
Why touch
Most robots and physical AI models rely on cameras alone. Vision shows a robot where things are, Lute’s founders wrote. It does not show how firmly the robot holds an item, whether the item is slipping or how fragile it is.
“We believe touch is the missing signal that lets robots handle real work reliably,” chief executive Paweł Budzianowski said in a statement published by FORWARD.one .
With partners, Lute co-designed small, soft tactile sensors and built them into a portable rig. That lets it collect touch data anywhere. Zurich’s Enact is chasing the same idea, and raised $30M in October to give robots a sense of touch.
Lute-0 against π0.5
Lute also released its first model, Lute-0. It learns from video how a scene changes and turns that into robot movements. It is the first of a family of models Lute plans to train on touch as well as vision.
In Lute’s own retail tests, Lute-0 matched or beat π0.5, the open-source model from Physical Intelligence . It handled vegetables successfully 76% of the time, against 22% for π0.5. With soft snacks, the score was 98% against 70%. Lute says it also responds twice as fast. The figures come from Lute’s internal evaluation, and TNW has seen no independent results.
Lute says Lute-0 was pre-trained on far less data than π0.5, and trained much faster. Its two lead investors give different figures. It used about a twentieth of the data and a quarter of the training steps, OTB Ventures wrote . FORWARD.one puts it at about a tenth of the pre-training data.
Robots on real sites
Ten months in, Lute’s models already work at what it calls Europe’s largest automotive parts distributor. OTB puts that company’s annual revenue at $6bn. Lute also works on site with large retailers, and its models run in hospital corridors, according to OTB. The startup also partners with integrators, the firms that install robots for clients, starting with healthcare and manufacturing.
On site, the robots work on their own where they can, and a remote operator steps in when one needs help. They run unattended about 90% of the time, according to FORWARD.one. Failures and fixes then go back into training, so each deployment improves the next.
“In physical AI, the slow and the perfect will both lose,” said Boy de Jonge, investment manager at FORWARD.one.
Budzianowski has a machine learning PhD from Cambridge and led the machine learning team at PolyAI. He also co-founded K-Scale Labs, which built low-cost open-source humanoid robots. Co-founder Krzysztof Walas, the chief technology officer, was an associate professor at Poznań University of Technology and advised the Polish warehouse robotics company Nomagic . The team has 16 people in Warsaw and the Bay Area.

articles.snippet: Sooner’s $20M Seed Gives Dubai First-Time Buyers Room for $272M in Home Purchases أراجيك - Arageek
articles.text:
Latest 🚀
Sooner’s $20M Seed Gives Dubai First-Time Buyers Room for $272M in Home Purchases
Dubai fintech Sooner raises $20M, led by Nuwa Capital and Amwal Capital Partners, to let first-time buyers pay 10% upfront instead of 20%.
By Abdelrahman Amr 28 November 2026 · 3 min read
Summary
Dubai fintech Sooner has raised $20 million in seed funding.
Nuwa Capital led $5 million in equity, with Amwal adding $15 million in debt.
Eligible buyers pay 10% upfront, with the rest spread over 60 monthly instalments.
The money can support around $272 million in home purchases during 2027.
A home equity line of credit and wider expansion are planned next.
Dubai-based fintech Sooner has raised $20 million in seed funding to grow its home financing service, which helps first-time buyers get onto the property ladder with a smaller upfront down payment. The round combines $5 million in equity led by Nuwa Capital with a $15 million Shariah-compliant debt facility from Amwal Capital Partners.
The idea is simple enough. Instead of finding the usual 20% of a property's value on day one, eligible buyers using Sooner's platform pay 10% upfront. The rest of the down payment is then spread across 60 equal Shariah-compliant monthly instalments, so over five years.
Joining Nuwa Capital on the equity side are 500 Global, Annex Investments, Plus VC, Serkal Group, Axeed Group, 21Ventures, Iliad Partners and a group of angel investors. That is a fairly broad table for a company that is still very young.
Sooner was founded in 2026 by Mohammed Aziz, Gabriel García Leyva and Vlad Cherevkov, and its platform is licensed by the Dubai Land Department. Alongside the down payment support, it offers digital mortgage pre-approvals and help with the property buying process itself.
The numbers since launch are worth a look. Sooner went live in July 2026 and has since received around 9,000 applications, representing $4.5 billion in prospective property purchases. It has already supported approximately $10 million in completed home purchases.
The new financing, the company says, gives it the capacity to support approximately $272 million in home purchases during 2027. That is a big jump from where it stands today, and the debt facility is clearly what makes that scale possible.
Why does this matter? First-time buyers in Dubai typically face a 20% down payment, plus closing costs of roughly 7% to 10%. For plenty of salaried residents, saving that lump sum is the real hurdle, not the monthly mortgage. To be fair, that is exactly the gap Sooner is going after.
Next on the roadmap is a home equity line of credit in 2027, which would let existing homeowners borrow against the equity in their properties. Further regional and international expansion is also planned.
The timing lines up with a busy market. Dubai's residential mortgage lending reached $5.9 billion in the third quarter of 2026, while the emirate's Real Estate Sector Strategy 2033 targets a 33% home-ownership rate.
Around Arageek, we often talk about fintechs that pick one painful moment in a customer's life and fix it properly. I reckon Sooner fits that pattern nicely. Pairing a regulated product with Shariah-compliant debt is a sensible way to grow a lending business in the Gulf, and if the 9,000 applications turn into completed purchases, this could become a useful model for housing finance across the region.

TELUS-Backed Taulia Raises $18M Series C Round
San Francisco-based Taulia Inc., a cloud-based payment and discounting solutions provider, has raised US$18 million in Series C financing. The deal involved an initial close of US$12.5 million led by German investor Klaus Hommels and Lakestar, with the participation of existing investors, including Matrix Partners, Trinity Ventures, TELUS Ventures and DAG Ventures. A secondary closing of US$5.5 million is underway. Earlier in August, Taulia entered into a strategic partnership with TELUS Corp. and its venture capital arm to expand the company's presence in Canada.

Reversa targets international expansion and sector-specific AI solutions
Reversa, a technology startup developing artificial intelligence agents for corporate and public-sector regulatory operations, has raised €750,000 in funding, including a pre-seed round led by Itnig, the investment fund established by Factorial’s founders.
Investors include the co-founders of Jobandtalent and business angels from the technology and legal sectors, including executives from HappyRobot, Fuse Energy, multinational banks and energy groups. The company also receives support from Enisa and CDTI’s Neotec programme.
Madrid-based Reversa has secured €750,000 in funding, including a pre-seed round led by Itnig, the investment fund of Factorial’s founders.
The company’s AI agents automate regulatory monitoring, legal research, compliance reviews and public affairs, reducing time spent on regulatory monitoring by 90% and regulatory analysis by 80%.
Reversa plans to expand its international regulatory infrastructure and develop specialized AI solutions for financial services, energy, real estate and urban planning.
Reversa solves regulatory problems for large companies and public institutions. To do so, it structures the regulation of each jurisdiction from its official sources, keeps it up to date and, on top of that infrastructure, builds specific solutions with artificial intelligence agents for different use cases.
Iñigo Martín Llorente, co-founder and CEO of Reversa
Founded in Madrid in 2025 by Tomás Burgaleta Alonso, Iñigo Martín Llorente and Santiago Aliaga Estella, Reversa describes its technology category as regulatory superintelligence.
AI agents automate regulatory compliance and legal workflows
Reversa’s regulatory radar connects AI agents directly to official regulatory sources, identifies how legislative changes affect individual companies and helps manage the steps required for implementation.
The platform addresses operational and commercial requirements, including identifying applicable legislation when entering new markets and automating compliance reviews for new products.
Other applications include jurisdiction-specific legal research, contract drafting and updates to corporate policies. Public affairs teams can anticipate regulatory developments, monitor legislative procedures in real time and participate in the legislative process.
Reversa’s customers include multinational corporations operating across multiple jurisdictions, Ibex 35 companies, public affairs consultancies and law firms.
Reversa is a regulatory system of action. It does not just capture information; it delivers the finished work. We build a digital replica of each jurisdiction, with its laws, institutions and procedures, and on top of it we automate workflows with agents that resolve our customers’ tasks end to end.
Santiago Aliaga Estella, co-founder and CTO
Multinational clients use the platform to coordinate regulatory monitoring across their markets, reduce compliance risks and generate a return on investment through a 90% reduction in time spent on regulatory monitoring and an 80% reduction in regulatory analysis time.

Lakshya Aerotech , the brand under which Lakshya SmartGuard Systems Private Limited operates, has raised ₹2.5 crore in seed funding from Santosh Kumar, promoter of Samkhyaa Group .
The company will use the investment to strengthen its research and development , engineering infrastructure, product development and indigenous manufacturing capabilities.
The company is focused on developing what it describes as indigenous physical intelligence technologies, which enable machines to perceive their surroundings, make decisions and interact autonomously with the physical world. Its work spans advanced engineering, embedded intelligence and autonomous systems, with an emphasis on converting core technologies into commercially deployable products.
Founded by Lokesh Popuri, Lakshya aims to build an engineering-driven deeptech business that develops and owns critical technologies for next-generation intelligent machines. Its stated areas of focus include research, embedded engineering, autonomous control, intellectual property development and domestic product manufacturing.
“Our decision to invest in Lakshya is driven by our conviction in the team's engineering capabilities, technological vision and ability to translate innovative ideas into tangible products,” said Santosh Kumar, promoter of Samkhyaa Group.
